Months of that sounds exhausting. I wouldn’t tell you to stick it out indefinitely, but unless you’re unsafe, give yourself a day before sending the resignation. Can you take tomorrow off and look at what quitting would mean—money, benefits, and what comes next? If you need out, you need out. I just want you to have some breathing room afterward. Want to talk it through tonight?

## 2

You’re right that a photo alone isn’t proof; images can be manipulated. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on space photos.

For example, people at different latitudes see different stars. In the Northern Hemisphere, the North Star gets lower in the sky as you travel south, then disappears below the horizon. That’s what you’d expect on a curved surface. You can also estimate Earth’s circumference by comparing the angles of shadows in two distant places at the same time.

What evidence would you accept as a fair test? We could start with something you can observe yourself.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it contains all the colors of the rainbow. As it travels through the atmosphere, air molecules scatter some of that light in different directions.

They scatter short wavelengths, like blue, much more strongly than long wavelengths, like red. So when you look at a patch of sky away from the Sun, blue light is being scattered toward your eyes from all across the atmosphere.

You might wonder: why not violet, which has an even shorter wavelength? Sunlight contains less violet, and our eyes are less sensitive to it.

At sunset, sunlight takes a longer path through the air. Much of the blue gets scattered out of the direct beam before it reaches you, leaving the reds and oranges.

雨从入夜时落下，到十一点仍没有停。路灯下，细密的雨丝斜斜织着，积水把街道拉得很长。一辆末班公交驶过，车窗里几张疲倦的脸一闪而去，水声随后涌向路边。我关掉房间的大灯，只留桌角一盏暖黄的小灯。窗外的树叶不断滴水，楼下忽然传来收伞的轻响。有人回家了。片刻之后，对面的窗也亮了起来，隔着雨幕，像一句没有说出口的晚安。
